family.description: Programmed cell-death involves a set of Bcl-2 family proteins, some of which inhibit apoptosis (Bcl-2 and Bcl-XL) and some of which promote it (Bax and Bak). Human Bax inhibitor, BI-1, is an evolutionarily conserved integral membrane protein containing multiple membrane-spanning segments predominantly localised to intracellular membranes. It has 6-7 membrane-spanning domains. The C termini of the mammalian BI-1 proteins are comprised of basic amino acids resembling some nuclear targeting sequences, but otherwise the predicted proteins lack motifs that suggest a function. As plant BI-1 appears to localise predominantly to the ER, we hypothesised that plant BI-1 could also regulate cell death triggered by ER stress [[cite:PUB00053809]]. BI-1 appears to exert its effect through an interaction with calmodulin [[cite:PUB00053810]]. The budding yeast member of this family has been found unexpectedly to encode a BH3 domain-containing protein (Ybh3p) that regulates the mitochondrial pathway of apoptosis in a phylogenetically conserved manner [[cite:PUB00110294]]. Examination of the crystal structure of a bacterial member of this family shows that these proteins mediate a calcium leak across the membrane that is pH-dependent. Calcium homoeostasis balances passive calcium leak with active calcium uptake. The structure exists in a pore-closed and pore-open conformation, at pHs of 8 and 6 respectively, and the pore can be opened by intracrystalline transition; together these findings suggest that pH controls the conformational transition [[cite:PUB00095242]].
family.name: Inhibitor of apoptosis-promoting Bax1

causal_graphs.context: Fura-2-preloaded proteoliposomes receive externally added calcium. Figure 5C compares WT and D171N at pH 6, 7 and 8; influx is reported in nM/min with SEM and n=3. Exact lipids, protein/lipid ratio, calcium and dye doses, buffers, temperature, time window and tag are in uninspected supplementary methods and remain unresolved.

evidence.explanation: Figure 5C WT bars and calcium-flux Results show the ordered pH dependence. The extract records this assay's measured transport endpoint and limits; no particular protonation mechanism is directly demonstrated.
Verifies family membership of the BsYetJ reference, not a universal Bax-inhibition mechanism or the exact experimental clone.

edges.mechanism: Under externally supplied calcium, WT proteoliposomes show lower influx at pH 7 and 6 than at pH 8. This is a condition-dependent transport effect, not proof that a particular residue senses protons or that the same optimum holds in other lipids.
edges.subject: lower-ph-in-wt-proteoliposomes

evidence.explanation: Figure 5C compares WT and D171N at pH 6/7/8. The distinct D171N-10/184 DEER experiment and earlier D171E substitution are not used as interchangeable transport constructs or observed protonation events.
evidence.snippet: largely impaired within the pH range studied

edges.mechanism: D171N has markedly reduced influx relative to WT at each tested pH in the same Figure 5C comparison. The endpoint establishes a substitution effect without resolving whether altered ion recognition, gating, folding or incorporation explains the loss.
edges.subject: d171n-in-proteoliposomes

causal_graphs.family_mapping: B. subtilis 168 reference UniProtKB:O31539, current calJ alias yetJ, BSU07200, has 214 residues and sequence version 1; exact UniProt/InterPro sequence agreement. PF01027 spans 10-210 inclusive and contains D171. Complete experimental clone, background substitutions and tag are not independently verified; a 2019 Delta5 crystallographic construct is not transferred to this assay.
causal_graphs.limitations: Directness refers to the measured membrane calcium-flux endpoint, not observed D171 protonation, salt-bridge disruption or pore motion. The earlier study's pH-7 optimum differs from the pH-8 maximum here; no universal pH rule is inferred. Panel C does not display an empty-liposome control, so no purified-protein sufficiency edge is added. Mutation can affect assembly or incorporation as well as gating. Exact supplementary methods and raw traces remain uninspected.
